newsitem.title: UK: OPEC reschedules output monitor meet for May in Iran.
newsitem.headline: OPEC reschedules output monitor meet for May in Iran.

text.p: OPEC has rescheduled a regular meeting of its quota compliance committee to take place in Isfahan, Iran in early May, an OPEC spokesman said on Friday.
The committee, which monitors OPEC output behaviour and usually meets four times a year, originally had planned to gather on Iran's Kish island in mid-March.
It has now been scheduled to take place either ahead of, or during, an oil and gas conference arranged by the National Iranian Oil Corp (NIOC) in Isfahan for May 8-10.
The committee is currently chaired by Iranian Oil Minister Gholamareza Aghazadeh with Nigeria's Dan Etete and Indonesia's Ida Bagus Sudjana. OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman will also attend.
OPEC's current president, Libyan Oil Minister Abdalla el-Badri, already has scheduled an appearance at the NIOC conference.

OPEC output in February ran some 1.74 million bpd in excess of the 11-member group's official 25.03 million bpd ceiling at 26.77 million, according to a Reuters survey, one of four independent estimates used by OPEC to monitor production trends.
By contrast member country submissions to OPEC headquarters put production in February at 25.33 million.
